title: Junction objects and many-to-many modeling
objectives: Explain a many-to-many model as two objects linked through a custom junction object that has two master-detail relationship fields.
Place attributes that belong to the pairing (role, dates, status) on the junction object, not on either master.
Describe cascade delete and sharing as following both masters, and treat JunctionIdList as a separate API convenience on some standard objects.
Refuse a single lookup when either side can have many of the other, and refuse two lookups when the business needs true master-detail junction behavior.
diagnostic_question: A property can have many vendors, and a vendor can serve many properties, with a unique contract start date per pairing. Is that a lookup, a master-detail, or a junction object—and where does the start date live?
definition: A many-to-many relationship lets each record of one object link to multiple records of another and vice versa. You model it by creating a custom junction object with two master-detail relationship fields, each pointing at one of the objects you want to relate. Custom objects with two master-detail relationships are supported in API version 11.0 and later. ([Relationships Among Standard Objects and Fields](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.object_reference.meta/object_reference/relationships_among_objects.htm); [Create a Many-to-Many Object Relationship](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.relationships_manytomany.htm))
why_it_matters: A single lookup or master-detail forces a one-to-many lie: either a property can have only one vendor, or a vendor only one property. Putting the contract date on Property or Vendor then overwrites the other pairings. Interviewers listen for a junction object with two master-detail fields and for pairing attributes living on the junction.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a concert ticket stub. The stub is useless unless it names both the attendee and the show. One attendee can hold many stubs; one show can have many stubs. The seat number and purchase time belong on the stub, not on the person or the show. In Salesforce the stub is a junction object with two required master-detail relationships. Tear up the attendee or the show and the stubs that bind them go with that master.
deeper_explanation: The Object Reference example: a custom Issue object related to Case so an issue can relate to multiple cases and a case to multiple issues. The implementation is a custom junction object with two master-detail fields. Help's many-to-many article is the administrator procedure for that pattern. ([Relationships Among Standard Objects and Fields](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.object_reference.meta/object_reference/relationships_among_objects.htm); [Create a Many-to-Many Object Relationship](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.relationships_manytomany.htm))

Because each link is master-detail, each junction row is a detail of both parents: it inherits sharing from the masters, has no independent Owner in the usual MD sense, and is deleted if either master is deleted. First versus second master (primary master) affects which master controls more of the sharing/ownership story—Needs verification of the current primary-master rules in Help before quoting extra detail.

Pairing attributes—role, status, start date, quantity—are fields on the junction object (DATA-002 types). Do not copy those values onto both masters. Related lists on each master show the junction rows (often displayed as the other master via the second relationship).

Starting in API 34.0, JunctionIdList lets some entities manipulate many-to-many links without touching junction rows directly. It is implemented on Task and Event, appears as an unbounded ID array in the WSDL, and is read-only in Apex. That is not a substitute for a custom junction object on LAB_ objects. ([Relationships Among Standard Objects and Fields](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.object_reference.meta/object_reference/relationships_among_objects.htm))

mental_model.analogy: A concert ticket stub that must name both the attendee and the show; seat and purchase time live on the stub, and tearing up either master invalidates the stub.
useful_mapping: first master-detail → attendee named on the stub
second master-detail → show named on the stub
pairing field → seat number or purchase time
related lists → stubs listed on the attendee and on the show
cascade from either master → cancel the person or the show and those stubs are deleted
JunctionIdList → a special backstage pass list on Task/Event, not your custom stub object
where_it_breaks: Two lookups can also model many-to-many without MD cascade; that is a different, looser design.
Primary versus secondary master sharing is more specific than a paper stub.
JunctionIdList on Task/Event is not how you build LAB_PropertyVendor__c.
A stub does not encode roll-up limits or data skew from one popular vendor.

teach_back_prompt: Explain why a property-to-vendor many-to-many needs a junction object, where the contract date lives, and what happens if you only put a lookup on Property.

telugu_glossary.telugu: Custom object with two master-detail fields that stores each pairing.

A field that describes only this link, not either parent.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Many-to-many uses a junction object with two master-detail fields. Pairing fields live on the junction. Deleting either master deletes the pairings. JunctionIdList is a Task/Event API feature, not your custom junction.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I name both parents and the pairing noun. Property-vendor-assignment is LAB_PropertyVendor__c with MD to Property and MD to Vendor. Contract start date goes on the junction. A Vendor lookup on Property would allow only one vendor. I mention cascade delete risk and data skew if one vendor is linked to tens of thousands of properties. I do not call a single lookup a junction.

terminology.plain: Each side can link to many of the other.
terminology.precise: A model where each record of one object links to multiple records of another and vice versa, implemented with a junction object.
terminology.example: A property served by many vendors; a vendor serving many properties.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: One-to-many lookup/MD: only one parent per child.
terminology.boundary: JunctionIdList is a special-case API, not the general model.

terminology.plain: The object that stores each pairing.
terminology.precise: A custom object with two master-detail relationship fields, each linking to one of the objects being related.
terminology.example: LAB_PropertyVendor__c with Property__c and Vendor__c MD fields.
terminology.non_example: A report joining two objects without a stored pairing row.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Intersection table in generic SQL: similar idea, Salesforce MD rules still apply.
terminology.boundary: API 11.0+ for two MD fields on a custom object.

terminology.plain: A field that describes this link, not either parent alone.
terminology.precise: A custom field on the junction object such as role, status, or start date.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Roll-up on a master: aggregates children, does not store the pairing.

terminology.plain: The first master-detail you create on the junction.
terminology.precise: The Object Reference notes ownership/sharing of a two-MD custom object is controlled by the master, or by the primary master when there are two. Exact UI order is Needs verification.
terminology.example: First MD to LAB_Property__c as primary master.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Secondary master: the other MD field.
terminology.boundary: Do not invent extra sharing percentages.

terminology.plain: An API field that edits some standard many-to-many links as a list of IDs.
terminology.precise: API 34.0+ field type on Task and Event; queries/updates act on underlying junction records; read-only in Apex.
terminology.example: Updating Event Who/related ID lists via JunctionIdList in the API.
terminology.non_example: Creating LAB_PropertyVendor__c rows in the UI.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Related list: UI, not the JunctionIdList type.
terminology.boundary: Do not use JunctionIdList as the design for custom objects.

terminology.plain: How each parent shows its pairings.
terminology.precise: Junction rows appear as related lists on both masters, often showing the other parent.
terminology.example: Vendors related list on a property via the junction.
terminology.non_example: A single lookup related list of properties on Vendor only.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Page layout: you still add the related list (DATA-009).
terminology.boundary: Labels are presentation, not the schema.

terminology.plain: Deleting either parent deletes the junction rows.
terminology.precise: Each MD field cascade-deletes details when that master is deleted.
terminology.example: Delete a vendor and its property-vendor stubs disappear.
terminology.non_example: Lookup children remaining after parent delete.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Recycle Bin restore of both masters: neighboring, org-sensitive.
terminology.boundary: Warn stakeholders before deleting a widely used vendor.

terminology.plain: Two lookups on a custom object instead of two master-details.
terminology.precise: A handbook heuristic when pairings must survive a parent delete or need their own Owner. Not the official Help procedure, which uses two MD fields.
terminology.example: LAB_PropertyVendor__c with two lookups if pairings must outlive a vendor merge.
terminology.non_example: Calling two lookups a master-detail junction.
terminology.boundary: Mark as design alternative; confirm sharing yourself.

when_to_use: When each record of object A can relate to many of object B and each B to many A—a many-to-many relationship.
When the link itself has fields (role, dates, status) that belong on a junction object, not on either parent.
When you need related lists of the other object on both parents through a custom junction object.
When explaining cascade delete: deleting either master deletes the junction pairings.
When an interviewer asks how Salesforce models many-to-many versus a single lookup or master-detail.
when_not_to_use: Do not use a junction object for a true one-to-many (units of a property)—that is a single relationship (DATA-003).
Do not put pairing attributes on the parent objects or in a text field of IDs (DATA-002).
Do not use JunctionIdList as the design for a custom property-vendor object; it is a Task/Event API type.
Do not treat a junction as a page-layout or record-type problem (DATA-008/009).
Do not park tens of thousands of junction rows under one dummy parent (DATA-005 skew).
configuration_or_code_location: Create custom junction object, then two Master-Detail fields on that object.
Add related lists on both parent page layouts.
Optional: unique rule or matching on the pair of relationship fields—Needs verification of current duplicate tools.
API: custom junction rows, not JunctionIdList, for LAB_ objects.

decision_table.signal: One property has many units; a unit has one property.
decision_table.choose: Single master-detail or lookup (DATA-003), not a junction.
decision_table.not: A junction object between property and unit.
decision_table.why: That grain is one-to-many, not many-to-many.

decision_table.signal: A property has many vendors and a vendor has many properties; the link has a start date.
decision_table.choose: Custom junction object with two master-detail fields; date on the junction.
decision_table.not: Vendor lookup on Property or start date on Vendor.
decision_table.why: Official many-to-many pattern plus pairing attributes on the junction.

decision_table.signal: You need to manipulate Task/Event many-to-many IDs in the API, not a custom object.
decision_table.not: A custom junction object named JunctionIdList__c.
decision_table.why: JunctionIdList is a field type on those standard objects from API 34.0.

decision_table.signal: Pairings must survive if a vendor record is deleted or merged.
decision_table.choose: Do not use two MD fields without a data-retention plan; consider a looser two-lookup design and mark sharing Needs verification.
decision_table.not: Standard two-MD junction while promising pairings will remain.
decision_table.why: MD cascade deletes junction rows when a master is deleted.

decision_table.signal: Someone stored comma-separated vendor IDs in a Text field on Property.
decision_table.choose: Replace with a junction object and relationship fields.
decision_table.not: Keep parsing the text in Flow.
decision_table.why: Text IDs are not relationship fields and cannot show proper related lists or cascade rules.

limitations: Primary-master sharing details are not fully specified here.
Does not teach roll-up of junction rows (DATA-007) or skew (DATA-005).
JunctionIdList coverage is limited to the Object Reference note.
Two-lookup alternative is a heuristic, not a Help mandate.
security_notes: Junction rows inherit master-detail sharing from their masters.
Deleting a widely shared vendor deletes pairings—treat as a data-loss event.
Do not hide a many-to-many in a text field of IDs that bypasses sharing.
common_mistakes: Putting a single lookup on one parent and calling it many-to-many.
Storing pairing dates on a master object.
Creating only one master-detail field on the junction.
Confusing JunctionIdList with a custom junction object.
Using a junction for a one-to-many unit model.

mcqs.prompt: How does the Object Reference say you create a many-to-many relationship?

options.A: A custom junction object with two master-detail relationship fields
options.B: Two lookup fields on each parent pointing at each other
options.C: A formula field listing child IDs
options.D: A JunctionIdList field on every custom object

mcqs.rationale: Create a custom junction object with two master-detail fields.

distractor_explanations.B: Mutual lookups are not the documented pattern.
distractor_explanations.D: JunctionIdList is not available on every custom object.

mcqs.prompt: From which API version are custom objects with two master-detail relationships supported?
mcqs.rationale: Custom objects with two MD relationships are supported in API 11.0 and later.

distractor_explanations.D: 67.0 is the current handbook API, not the introduction version.

mcqs.prompt: Where should a contract start date that is unique per property-vendor pair live?

options.D: In a validation rule with no field

mcqs.rationale: Pairing attributes belong on the junction object.

distractor_explanations.B: One date on Vendor overwrites other properties.
distractor_explanations.C: One date on Property overwrites other vendors.
distractor_explanations.D: A validation rule does not store the date.

mcqs.prompt: JunctionIdList is implemented on which objects in the Object Reference note?
mcqs.rationale: JunctionIdList is implemented in the Task and Event objects.

mcqs.prompt: Can Apex set a new value on an existing JunctionIdList field?

options.A: No. All JunctionIdLists are read-only in Apex

mcqs.rationale: All JunctionIdLists are read-only in Apex; setting a new value throws an exception.

distractor_explanations.C: The feature is on Task/Event, not custom objects.
distractor_explanations.D: Validation rules are not how you set JunctionIdList.

mcqs.prompt: A property lookup on Vendor is the only link. What grain did you actually model?

options.A: Many vendors per... no: one property per vendor (many-to-one), not many-to-many

mcqs.rationale: A single lookup gives each vendor one property, not many properties per vendor and many vendors per property.

distractor_explanations.B: A junction needs two relationship fields on a third object.
distractor_explanations.C: One lookup is not two-way MD.

mcqs.prompt: What happens to junction rows if either master is deleted?

options.A: Those detail/junction rows are deleted with that master
options.D: They move to the Recycle Bin of the other master only

mcqs.rationale: Master-detail cascade deletes details when that master is deleted.

distractor_explanations.D: Do not invent Recycle Bin ownership here.

mcqs.prompt: Units of a property: one property, many units, each unit one property. Junction?

options.A: No. That is one-to-many; use a single relationship on Unit
options.B: Yes, always use a junction for any parent-child
options.D: Yes, with two lookups on Property

mcqs.rationale: One-to-many is DATA-003, not a junction.

distractor_explanations.C: JunctionIdList is not for this custom model.
distractor_explanations.D: Two lookups on Property cannot express unit grain cleanly.

mcqs.prompt: In the Object Reference Issue/Case example, what allows a case to have many issues and an issue many cases?

options.A: A custom junction object with two master-detail fields
options.D: Changing Case to a custom object

mcqs.rationale: The documented example uses a junction object with two MD fields.

distractor_explanations.B: A checkbox is not a relationship.
distractor_explanations.C: A formula does not create pairings.
distractor_explanations.D: Case remaining standard is fine; the junction is custom.

mcqs.prompt: Who gets the two master-detail fields?

options.B: Each parent object gets one MD to the other parent

mcqs.rationale: Both MD fields are created on the junction object.

distractor_explanations.B: Parents do not MD to each other directly in this pattern.
distractor_explanations.D: Report types consume the model; they do not create it.

mcqs.prompt: Why is JunctionIdList the wrong answer for LAB_PropertyVendor__c?

options.A: JunctionIdList is a Task/Event API field type, not a custom junction object
options.B: JunctionIdList cannot be mentioned in interviews

mcqs.rationale: The Object Reference limits JunctionIdList to Task/Event and describes it as an ID-array field type.

distractor_explanations.B: You may mention it as a boundary.
distractor_explanations.D: It does not replace custom MD junctions.

mcqs.prompt: A standard object cannot be the detail of a custom master. How does that affect a junction?

options.A: Each MD on the junction must still obey that eligibility rule
options.C: You should MD from Lead to a custom junction as Lead-detail
options.D: Only JunctionIdList can relate standard objects

mcqs.rationale: Each master-detail field still has eligibility constraints.

distractor_explanations.C: Lead-as-detail of custom is the blocked pattern.
distractor_explanations.D: Standard-to-standard many-to-many is not only JunctionIdList.

interview_questions.question: How do you model many-to-many in Salesforce?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Create a custom junction object with two master-detail relationship fields, each pointing at one parent. Pairing fields go on the junction. Supported on custom objects in API 11.0+.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I name both parents and the pairing noun. I refuse a single lookup. I mention cascade delete from either master and related lists on both sides. I distinguish JunctionIdList on Task/Event from this custom-object pattern. I do not invent unofficial junction limits.
interview_questions.example: LAB_PropertyVendor__c with MD to Property and MD to Vendor.
follow_ups: Where does the contract date go?
weak_answer_warnings: Putting two MD fields on the parents

interview_questions.question: Property has many vendors and vendor has many properties. A teammate adds Vendor lookup on Property. What do you say?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: That model allows only one vendor per property. We need a junction object so both sides can have many, and so the contract date can live on the pairing.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I draw two example rows: vendor Acme on Property 1 and 2; Property 1 also has vendor Beta. A lookup cannot store both. I create LAB_PropertyVendor__c with two MD fields. I migrate any existing single-vendor data as a first pairing row. I warn that deleting a vendor deletes pairings.
interview_questions.example: Rejected Property.Vendor__c lookup; created three junction rows in sandbox.
tradeoffs: Migrate one lookup vs start over
follow_ups: How do you stop duplicate pairings?
How do reports list vendors per property?
weak_answer_warnings: Accepting the lookup as good enough

interview_questions.question: Where do you put the role and start date for each pairing?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: On the junction object as typed custom fields. Putting them on Vendor or Property overwrites other pairings.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: This is a DATA-002 type choice on a DATA-004 object. Date for start, picklist for role. I do not create formula copies on both parents unless there is a later denormalization reason (DATA-005/006). Related lists show the pairing fields if the layout includes them.
tradeoffs: Normalize onto junction vs stamp onto parent
follow_ups: Can you roll up the latest start date?
Should role be a record type?
weak_answer_warnings: Storing the date on both parents

interview_questions.question: What is JunctionIdList and when is it the wrong answer?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: An API 34.0+ field type on Task and Event that exposes many-to-many IDs as an array. It is read-only in Apex. It is the wrong design for a custom junction object.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I only mention it so I do not confuse interviewers who saw it in the Object Reference. Custom many-to-many still uses a junction object and junction records. I would not tell an admin to 'add a JunctionIdList field' on LAB_PropertyVendor__c.
interview_questions.example: Event relations via JunctionIdList versus LAB_PropertyVendor__c rows in Object Manager.
follow_ups: Can you query it like a field?
weak_answer_warnings: Using JunctionIdList as the definition of junction object

interview_questions.question: Deleting a vendor wiped property-vendor history. Was that a bug?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Not if the junction used master-detail. Deleting a master deletes detail/junction rows. That is documented cascade behavior.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I confirm both fields are MD. I explain the ticket-stub analogy: cancel the performer and those stubs are void. If history must survive vendor delete, the model should not have been two MD fields, or the vendor should have been deactivated rather than deleted. I do not restore production data from this lesson.
interview_questions.example: Sandbox: delete LAB_Vendor__c Acme and watch LAB_PropertyVendor__c rows for Acme disappear.
tradeoffs: Two MD vs two lookups for history
follow_ups: How do you recover junction rows?
Does deleting Property also delete pairings?
weak_answer_warnings: Calling cascade delete a platform bug

interview_questions.question: When is a junction the wrong model?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When the grain is one-to-many, when you only need a single parent pointer, or when you are trying to use JunctionIdList on a custom object.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Units of a property are one-to-many. A single optional vendor is a lookup. Task/Event ID arrays are JunctionIdList, not LAB_PropertyVendor__c. I also refuse a junction that exists only to work around a page-layout or record-type problem. If pairings must outlive a parent, I flag two-MD cascade as a risk.

interview_questions.question: The Vendors related list is missing on Property. How do you debug the junction?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Check that the junction object has both master-detail fields and that the junction related list was added to the property page layout. A missing list is often presentation, not a missing object.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I open Object Manager on LAB_PropertyVendor__c and confirm two MD fields. I open the Property page layout and add the related list. I create a LAB_ pairing and refresh. If the second MD was never created, I am still in a one-to-many. I do not rebuild the junction until those two checks fail.
interview_questions.example: Added the Property Vendors related list to the LAB_Property__c layout after confirming two MD fields.

interview_questions.question: How do master-detail eligibility rules still apply to a junction?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Each master-detail field on the junction must still obey deletion, Owner, and standard-object-as-detail rules. A junction does not waive those constraints.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: If one parent is a custom object, a standard object still cannot sit as that MD detail in the blocked pattern. I create both MD fields on the junction, not on the parents. I mention API 11.0+ for two MD fields. I keep JunctionIdList out of the custom-object design.
interview_questions.example: Junction LAB_CaseIssue__c with MD to Case and MD to LAB_Issue__c only after confirming each side is an allowed pair.
